mappings.note: Importance of DNA copying = it carries the parental body-design blueprint into the offspring. That is the heredity mechanism of C 3.3, not C 3.3-LO-1, which is only about sexual reproduction out-varying asexual; no mode comparison is asked.
Asks why variation helps the SPECIES though not the individual - the value of variation, not a sexual-vs-asexual comparison, so C 3.3 and not C 3.3-LO-1.
Binary vs multiple fission: two asexual modes contrasted. C 3.2-LO-6 names fission explicitly; nothing here touches plants (LO-7) or variation (C 3.3-LO-1).

Benefit of spore formation - an asexual mode and its survival advantage (thick-walled spores, many offspring). C 3.2-LO-6 covers asexual modes; not C 3.3-LO-1 because no comparison with sexual variation is demanded.
Why regeneration cannot build a new complex individual - limits of an asexual mode tied to cell specialisation. C 3.2-LO-6, not C 4.2 (no human organ system in play).
Why vegetative propagation is practised - vegetative propagation is named verbatim in C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7: no pollination/fertilisation/seed step is involved, which is the whole point.
DNA copying as the essential event of reproduction - the DNA/heredity mechanism of C 3.3. C 3.3-LO-1 is rejected: the answer does not rest on sexual reproduction varying more than asexual.
Pollination vs fertilisation is the first-to-second step of C 3.2-LO-7's own sequence. Not LO-6: both processes belong to sexual reproduction in flowering plants.

Seminal vesicles and prostate are named parts of the human male tract and the question asks their function - the exact demand of C 4.2-LO-4. Not LO-5: nothing about contraception or reproductive health.

Secondary sexual characters at puberty in girls. C 4.2-LO-4 covers parts and their functions, which this does not ask; LO-5 is family planning. No outcome reaches puberty, so the honest level is the competency C 4.2.
Embryo nourishment = the placenta, a structure of the pregnant uterus, and its function. Straight C 4.2-LO-4; not LO-5, which is family planning/reproductive health.
Copper-T vs sexually transmitted disease protection - a family-planning device judged against reproductive health, which is exactly C 4.2-LO-5. Not LO-4: no organ function is asked.
Identifies budding (yeast) among four organisms - budding is named in C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7 or C 4.2; all four options are unicellular asexual reproducers.
Picks vas deferens as NOT female - pure part-identification in the human reproductive system, C 4.2-LO-4.
Anther contains pollen grains - a flower part in the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7. Not C 4.2-LO-4, which is the HUMAN system.

Advantages of sexual over asexual reproduction rest entirely on greater variation and adaptability - C 3.3-LO-1 verbatim. Not C 3.2-LO-6, which only asks the student to distinguish and describe the modes, not to justify one.
Functions of the testis (sperm production + testosterone) - a named human reproductive part and its function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Why menstruation occurs = the prepared uterine lining breaks down when no zygote implants; that is the uterus's function, C 4.2-LO-4. Not LO-5: menstruation is not a family-planning method.
Methods of contraception is the literal content of C 4.2-LO-5. Not LO-4: no organ is named.
Unicellular vs multicellular modes of reproduction - fission/budding against the specialised-tissue modes. C 3.2-LO-6 is the outcome that distinguishes the modes.

Why reproduction stabilises a species' population. No outcome in this frame covers the purpose of reproduction as a life process; C 3.2 is the competency that names reproduction, so it is the most specific TRUE code.
Reasons for adopting contraception - family planning rationale, C 4.2-LO-5. Not LO-4: no part or function is asked.
Bartholin's glands belong to the FEMALE tract - part identification, C 4.2-LO-4. (Stored concept tag says 'Human Male Reproductive System', which is wrong.)

Stem is 'What does the diagram depict' with no figure available; nothing identifiable is being tested, so only the chapter competency C 3.2 can honestly be claimed. Flagged as figure-dependent/unanswerable.
Stem is 'Identify the material shown in the diagram' with no figure; no outcome can be verified. Competency level only. Flagged as unanswerable.
Bryophyllum multiplies by buds in leaf notches - vegetative propagation, named in C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7: no flower, pollen or seed involved.
When menstruation is absent (before puberty, pregnancy, after menopause) - the uterine/ovarian cycle's normal function, C 4.2-LO-4. Not LO-5.

Normal fertility period = the span between puberty and menopause during which the ovary releases eggs; a function of the reproductive organs, C 4.2-LO-4. Not LO-5, which is about planning methods, not reproductive span.

Labels parts A-E of the female tract and asks where egg production, fertilisation and implantation occur, plus uterine-lining changes - all part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4. Part (a) depends on a figure not present.
Fruit formed although stamens were removed => pollen arrived from another flower (cross-pollination). Reasoning sits in the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7, not LO-6.
Whether cell division counts as reproduction in unicellular organisms - the fission case of C 3.2-LO-6. Not C 3.3: no DNA/chromosome mechanism is demanded.

Clone definition plus why asexual offspring are near-identical; answerable only by contrasting the (absent) variation of asexual reproduction with sexual reproduction - C 3.3-LO-1. Not C 3.2-LO-6, which asks only for the modes.

Parents and sexually produced offspring carry the same chromosome number because gametes are halved and restored at fertilisation - a chromosome mechanism, so C 3.3 rather than C 3.3-LO-1 (no variation comparison).
Yeast buds only when nutrients are present - the conditions under which an asexual mode operates, C 3.2-LO-6.
Bread mould needs moisture for its spores to germinate and grow - conditions for an asexual mode, C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7: Rhizopus is not a flowering plant.
Two reasons variation appears in sexually produced progeny (gamete fusion from two parents, DNA-copying errors) - exactly why sexual reproduction out-varies asexual, C 3.3-LO-1.
Whether a vertically halved Planaria regenerates two individuals - regeneration/fragmentation, the asexual modes of C 3.2-LO-6.
Chromosome number vs organism size and DNA content - chromosome/DNA mechanism, C 3.3. Not C 3.3-LO-1: no sexual-vs-asexual variation argument.
Chromosome counts in gamete and zygote of tobacco - haploid/diploid arithmetic, C 3.3. Not LO-7, although the organism is a plant: nothing about pollination or seed formation is asked.
Fertilisation is impossible without pollination because the pollen must first reach the stigma - the pollination-to-fertilisation link of C 3.2-LO-7.
Constancy of chromosome number across zygote, embryonal cells and adult, maintained by mitosis and by meiosis at gamete formation - C 3.3 chromosome mechanism, not the variation comparison of LO-1.
The zygote lies in the ovule inside the ovary after fertilisation - the fertilisation-to-seed step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Reproduction and population stability. Same as qid:86115: no learning outcome covers the purpose of reproduction, so C 3.2 (the competency naming reproduction) is the most specific true code.
General growth vs sexual maturation - puberty. C 4.2-LO-4 is parts-and-functions and LO-5 is family planning; neither reaches sexual maturation, so the competency C 4.2 is the honest level.
Traces the sperm's path and the accessory glands' functions - a part-by-part account of the human male tract, C 4.2-LO-4.
Uterine changes when fertilisation fails (lining sheds) - function of the uterus, C 4.2-LO-4.
Uterine changes after implantation (lining thickens, placenta forms) - function of the uterus, C 4.2-LO-4.
Benefits of mechanical barriers - contraception plus protection from infection, both sides of C 4.2-LO-5. Not LO-4: no organ function is asked.
Names the female parts responsible for egg production, fertilisation, implantation and sperm entry - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Egg-to-zygote chromosome ratio and how a sperm differs genetically (X or Y) - chromosome mechanism, C 3.3, not the variation comparison of C 3.3-LO-1.
Why budding, fragmentation and regeneration are asexual, plus regeneration in Planaria - budding and fragmentation are named in C 3.2-LO-6.

Two-part: differences between asexual and sexual reproduction (C 3.2-LO-6) AND why sexually produced offspring vary (C 3.3-LO-1). The second half cannot be answered from LO-6 alone, so both are cited.
Pollination vs fertilisation, site and product of fertilisation, pollen-tube diagram - the full C 3.2-LO-7 sequence.
Gamete vs zygote and their roles - the defining machinery of sexual reproduction, which C 3.2-LO-6 distinguishes from asexual. Not C 3.3: no chromosome counting or variation argument is required.
Four whorls of a flower and the gamete-producing organs - flower structure underpinning C 3.2-LO-7. Not C 4.2-LO-4, which is the human system.
Placenta and its role in pregnancy - a structure of the pregnant uterus and its function, C 4.2-LO-4. Not LO-5: pregnancy support is not family planning.
Ways to avoid pregnancy, one elaborated - contraceptive methods, C 4.2-LO-5.
How fertilisation takes place and why only once a month - the ovulation/fertilisation function of ovary and oviduct, C 4.2-LO-4.
Reproduction is for species stability, not individual survival. No outcome covers the purpose of reproduction; C 3.2 is the competency that names it.
Sexually transmitted diseases and their prevention - reproductive health, the second half of C 4.2-LO-5.
Counselling a couple against further children and giving guidelines - family planning at the family level, C 4.2-LO-5.
Propagating Bougainvillea around a campus means taking cuttings - vegetative propagation, named in C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7: no seed route is used.
Falling sex ratio, its causes and remedies - reproductive health at the social level, C 4.2-LO-5. Not LO-4.
AIDS as a sexually transmitted disease, its causative organism and public awareness programmes - reproductive health, C 4.2-LO-5.
Expanding HIV - recall inside the STD/reproductive-health strand of C 4.2-LO-5.
Expanding IUCD - a named contraceptive device, C 4.2-LO-5.
Type of fission in Amoeba (binary, any plane) - fission is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Definition of vegetative propagation - named verbatim in C 3.2-LO-6.
Two functions of the ovary (ovum release + hormone secretion) - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Effect of imperfect DNA copying = variations appear. That is the DNA-mechanism claim of C 3.3; C 3.3-LO-1 is narrower and would require the sexual-vs-asexual comparison, which is not asked.

Names the hormone (oestrogen) whose secretion drives the changes in girls - i.e. the ovary's endocrine function, which C 4.2-LO-4 covers. Preferred over the bare-puberty items mapped to C 4.2 because the answer is an organ's secretion.
Common mode of reproduction in Amoeba and Planaria (fission, regeneration) - asexual modes, C 3.2-LO-6.
Name two types of asexual reproduction - directly the enumeration in C 3.2-LO-6.
Rose is grown from stem cuttings/grafting - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7 despite being a flowering plant: the method deliberately bypasses pollination and seed.
Jasmine is grown by layering/cuttings - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6.
Why no two individuals in a population are alike - variation arising from DNA-copying errors and recombination. C 3.3 rather than C 3.3-LO-1, since the question never sets sexual against asexual.
Justifying that cell division IS reproduction in unicellular organisms - the fission case of C 3.2-LO-6.
Names the mode that involves gametes and the one that does not - the sexual/asexual distinction of C 3.2-LO-6.
Define puberty. No outcome in this frame covers sexual maturation (LO-4 is parts and functions, LO-5 is family planning), so C 4.2 is the most specific true code.
Names reproduction as the life process behind population growth - no outcome covers the role of reproduction; C 3.2 is the competency that names it.
Two simple organisms that regenerate - an asexual mode, C 3.2-LO-6. Not C 4.2: no human system involved.
Where DNA sits in the cell (nucleus/chromosomes) - the molecular basis of heredity, C 3.3. Not LO-1: no variation comparison.
Mode of reproduction commonest in unicellular organisms (fission) - C 3.2-LO-6.
Definition of sexual reproduction - the sexual side of the C 3.2-LO-6 distinction. Not C 3.3-LO-1, which would demand the variation argument.
Site of fertilisation in the human female (fallopian tube) - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Parts of a flower housing the germ cells (anther, ovule) - flower structure in the C 3.2-LO-7 sequence.
Bryophyllum's leaf notches bear the propagating buds - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6.
What DNA is - the molecule of heredity, C 3.3. LO-1 rejected: no sexual-vs-asexual variation claim.
Cut Planaria pieces regenerate - regeneration, an asexual mode under C 3.2-LO-6.
Hydra reproduces by budding, and the student must say the mode is asexual - budding is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Two unisexual flowers - flower type, part of the pollination context of C 3.2-LO-7. Not C 4.2-LO-4: these are plants.
Fertilisation impossible without pollination - the C 3.2-LO-7 sequence.
A long Spirogyra filament breaks into fragments - fragmentation, named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Organisms carrying both sex organs (hermaphrodites) with an example - an organisation of sexual reproduction, sitting with the sexual/asexual distinction of C 3.2-LO-6 rather than with plant LO-7.
Two functions of the human ovary - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Spirogyra reproduces by fragmentation under favourable conditions, and the mode is asexual - C 3.2-LO-6.
Planaria reproduces by regeneration, asexual - C 3.2-LO-6.
Plasmodium reproduces by multiple fission, asexual - fission is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
What happens to a cell's DNA when it reproduces (it is copied first) - the DNA mechanism of C 3.3, not the variation comparison of LO-1.
Why DNA copies are sometimes not identical - copying errors, C 3.3.
Why variation matters to a species - the value of variation, C 3.3. Not C 3.3-LO-1: no comparison between reproductive modes is asked.
Names testes and ovaries as the organs producing the human germ cells - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Definition of fertilisation and its site in the human female (oviduct) - C 4.2-LO-4. Not LO-7: humans, not flowers.
Two differences between pollination and fertilisation - the two steps named in C 3.2-LO-7.
